eva: Hey — quick one. We're seeing different cancellation behaviour across SDKs when a client aborts a streaming generation. Browser + Node + Python all differ. Anyone seen a concise pattern we should recommend in the SDK docs? Example: client aborts after first token, server sometimes keeps generating (wasteful) or the Node stream emits an error, but Python gets a clean interruption. Thoughts?

sam: I ran into this. TL;DR: treat cancellation as "best-effort" in docs, and provide a clear client-side handshake example for each runtime. Node's stream.destroy vs AbortController semantics are messy.

niko: Useful checklist:
- Browser fetch with AbortController -> network request stops, server may still finish work
- Node fetch (undici) + AbortController -> signal usually closes socket, stream emits "aborted" error
- Native streaming libs (gRPC/websocket) -> require explicit close/ping in protocol
- Python requests/HTTPX -> close response iterator, server often sees connection close faster

maya: For docs we should show code snippets for idiomatic cancellation patterns and mention cost/regression implications. E.g. Node example:

```js
const ac = new AbortController();
fetch(url, { signal: ac.signal })
  .then(res => {
    const reader = res.body.getReader();
    // read loop...
  })
// later
ac.abort(); // reader will error/stop in Node + browser
```

sam: Also add example for SDK streaming wrapper: expose a cancel() that does both ac.abort() and stream.destroy() for Node. That covers both fetch-based and net-socket-based transports.

niko: On retries: if a user aborts, do NOT auto-retry by default. That's surprising to apps (double-side effects). Instead: make retry on client-configurable and require idempotency keys when enabling aggressive retries.

eva: Good call. What about server-side handling? We shouldn't assume a closed TCP = stop compute. We need guidance for ops teams.

maya: Server note: connection close is a signal, but background work may continue. Recommend lightweight early cancellation hooks in model runtime that check token generation loop for connection liveness every N tokens. Also safe shutdown windows (e.g., 100ms grace) before freeing GPU to avoid state corruption.

sam: For SDK tests, add a flaky test that simulates network drop mid-stream and assert SDK exposes a cancellable error event and that cancel() is idempotent.

niko: One more interop wrinkle: languages with GC (Go, Node) sometimes drop the AbortController object if not held strongly; docs should show lifecycle: keep ac in closure until stream fully settled.

ci-bot: FYI: I'll add a checklist PR template: "streaming cancellation docs", "retry idempotency guidance", "server cancellation hook". Will ping reviewers.

eva: Perfect — can someone assemble the three code examples (browser, node, python) and a short blurb about server best-effort cancellation? I'll open a tiny RFC.

maya: I'll draft the client snippets.

sam: I'll handle the Node edge-case notes and the SDK cancel() wrapper.

niko: I'll add the server runtime checks and the flaky test harness.

eva: Thanks all :thumbsup!
